Status

FinKore Core 2.0.4 stable.

Purpose

Approvals describes required business decisions and the evidence that makes them effective for a particular subject and set of facts.

Authorization answers, “May this Actor perform this operation?” Approval answers, “Has the required business decision been granted?” Authorization to perform an operation must not be treated as evidence that an Approval Requirement is satisfied.

Documents

Start with requirements and conditions, then decisions and validity. Read chains for sequential or unordered combinations, and composition for groups, quorum, and stages.

DocumentWhat you will learn
RequirementsThe subject, eligible decision-makers, and required outcome
ConditionsWhether a Requirement applies to the supplied facts
DecisionsRecorded outcomes, scoped identity, and fact association
ValidityWhether a historical Decision remains effective now
ChainsCombining Requirements sequentially or without ordering
CompositionAll-of, any-of, quorum, and staged evaluation with limited nesting
ErrorsPortable failure codes and composition validation priority

Composition fixture labels are conformance-local; they are not canonical Agentic operations.

Requirements

  • Approval behavior must be based on declared Approval Requirements.
  • An Approval Decision must identify its Approval Requirement, outcome, Actor, time, and association with the relevant subject state or facts.
  • An Approval Chain must define how its Approval Requirements combine and must declare sequencing only when sequencing applies.
  • Approval Composition combines Requirements through bounded all-of, any-of, quorum, staged, and nested groups. Its detailed rules cover applicability, voter evidence, thresholds, actionability, and complete validation.
  • Conditional Approval Requirements must use explicit domain facts.
  • Approval Validity must derive current effectiveness from append-only history, explicit evaluation context, relevant subject facts or revisions, and lifecycle evidence such as withdrawal, expiration, or supersession.

Sequential Chain actionability follows the first non-approved Requirement. Concrete Decision/history boundaries reject caller-asserted effectiveness and validate eligibility across all supplied Decisions for the evaluated Requirement. Approval Composition retains its separate lightweight current-effectiveness observation contract.

Invariants

An Approval outcome must be derivable from the applicable Approval Requirements and effective Approval Decisions.

Non-Goals

This domain does not define RBAC, authentication, organizational directories, UI inboxes, notification delivery, delegation, escalation, approval-definition migration, dynamic approver resolution, arbitrary dependency graphs, or unrestricted workflow engines.
